transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ariana Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Susan Park (CTO, Riverside), Michael Torres (Head of AI), Leah Chen (Infra), Jordan Rivera (PM)

00:00:00 - Ariana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ariana with Redwood Inference, i'll hand off to Marcus for the product walkthrough in a few minutes. lots on the agenda but mainly model catalog and how you pick open models for clinical nlp.
00:00:18 - Michael: thanks, appreciate it. quick note, we're on a tight timeline, looking to pilot in q3, probably July timeline.
00:00:27 - Dr. Park: yes timeline is roughly quarter 3, also need to make sure data residency and SOC2 compliance checks happen up front.
00:00:35 - Ariana: totally understood, we'll touch on security and also the private deployment options. Marcus?
00:00:40 - Marcus: cool thanks. so i'll share my screen, this is the model catalog UI. right here you can filter by task \u2014 generation, chat, embeddings, rerank \u2014 and by the curated open models we verify. some transcription note: the UI says "compatability" sometimes in the auto transcript so apologies if spelling odd.
00:01:02 - [00:01:02] Marcus: For Riverside's use case you flagged clinical note summarization and entity extraction. we typically recommend starting with a few open LLMs that have strong medical finetunes or instruction-tuned variants. on the right we surface benchmark cards \u2014 latency, 99th p95 token cost, and eval results on prompt sets.
00:01:30 - Jordan: are those evals public or internal? can we bring our own eval sets?
00:01:36 - Marcus: good Q. the cards show our internal perf profiles but you can upload your own eval sets \u2014 we run them on dedicated or hosted endpoints and return a compatibility matrix showing quantization and hardware support.
00:01:53 - [00:01:53] Marcus: example: "MedLite-7B" has been verified at int8 on A100 and on Ampere-based instances, it supports our fast-kv path, but for longer sequences you might want an L3 kernel; the compatibility matrix will flag where we expect degraded perf with aggressive quantization. note, the transcript sometimes says "kay vee cash" for KV cache \u2014 that's the ASR glitch.
00:02:18 - Michael: curious about hallucinations \u2014 do you have quality metrics tied to the benchmarks?
00:02:23 - Marcus: yes, we show rouge/bleu-ish metrics and custom hallucination checks tied to your prompt set. we also track regression alerts over time. for clinical we recommend a higher-precision run for sensitive outputs, or a reranker/verification pass using embeddings + semantic search.
00:02:45 - Dr. Park: on deployment, we're leaning private due to PHI. can you summarize the differences between private and dedicated for latency and cost?
00:02:55 - Marcus: short answer: private gives you a customer-managed control plane (VPC peering, customer KMS/HSM), so lower data egress risk and compliance envelope; dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved capacity with data isolation but within our control plane \u2014 a little faster to stand up and lower ops burden. cost-wise private is higher due to infra and infra ops; dedicated is middle ground; hosted is cheapest to start.
00:03:20 - [00:03:20] Marcus: we also provide a cost/perf planner in the Optimize tab \u2014 it suggests quant profiles and batching parameters per route. for example, for MedLite-7B we recommend int8 batch of 8 on A100 for 'care-summary' route and int4 if you can accept higher variance but lower cost. the planner also shows expected token cost.
00:03:44 - Leah: how accurate are quant recommendations for clinical text? int4 on medical jargon seems risky.
00:03:50 - Marcus: agreed, int4 is aggressive. the compatibility matrix will run your prompt set and give a pass/fail or caution. we generally advise int8 for clinical by default, with a verify-run at int4 if you want to squeeze costs.
00:04:05 - [00:04:05] Jordan: what's the benchmarking turnaround? if we upload 500 test prompts how long until we get results?
00:04:11 - Marcus: time depends on scale and whether you pick hosted or dedicated. hosted quick demo run is typically <24 hours, a full dedicated benchmark (large evals with variants) might take 48-72 hours. we'll include a benchmark runbook in the follow-up.
00:04:30 - [00:04:30] Michael: and about model selection \u2014 is there an automated recommendation engine?
00:04:34 - Marcus: yes, the catalog has a recommendation engine that uses your workload profile (seq lengths, qps, success criteria) it ranks models by a score combining latency, cost, and quality on your evals. it's not perfect but it surfaces a shortlist \u2014 usually 2-4 candidates.
00:04:52 - [00:04:52] Ariana: in your stack what do you currently use for embeddings and vector store?
00:04:57 - Michael: we have an in-house vector store using Milvus and embedding models from Cohere for now. exploring moving embeddings onto the same infra to reduce cross-cloud egress.
00:05:10 - Marcus: we support direct integration with Milvus and most vector stores; embeddings can be generated via Redwood endpoints and piped into your store. that reduces egress and simplifies auth.
00:05:24 - [00:05:24] Marcus: jumping back to the compatibility matrix, here's a sample matrix (we referenced a shared spreadsheet earlier). columns include model, quant options (fp16,int8,int4), tested hardware, expected latency at median and p95, and notes on sequence-length regressions.
00:05:45 - Dr. Park: would you run these on our on-prem GPUs too? we have some older V100 clusters.
00:05:51 - Marcus: we can run if you allow a connectivity window or we can run an identical config in our private sandbox with emulated V100 profiles. the matrix will show where kernels are unsupported \u2014 older CUDA versions sometimes break int8 paths.
00:06:10 - [00:06:10] Jordan: security \u2014 can you confirm SSO and audit logs integration?
00:06:14 - Ariana: yes, Redwood supports SAML/SSO, SCIM, RBAC and we provide audit logs, request-level tracing, and long-term retention as an add-on. for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management.
00:06:30 - Michael: data retention \u2014 we need strict no-persist on hosted. is that possible?
00:06:35 - Marcus: hosted with no-persist is available, but some customers prefer dedicated/private for full control. no-persist means we don't keep input payloads beyond ephemeral caches and logs still have to align on monitoring needs.
00:06:50 - [00:06:50] Marcus: demo note: sometimes transcripts miss the model names; you might see "redwood verified med light" instead of "MedLite" in the ASR.
00:07:05 - Marcus: show the model detail page: here's training details, license, quantization friendliness, kernel preferences, and known failure modes. we also surface a column for "legal friendliness" \u2014 is the base license permissive for commercial use \u2014 and whether any downstream fine-tune requirements exist.
00:07:30 - [00:07:30] Michael: ok on licenses \u2014 we need to be careful about derivative restrictions. is that flagged?
00:07:36 - Marcus: yes, license flags are in the model meta; we can also include an internal legal summary for models you shortlist.
00:07:45 - [00:07:45] Marcus: switching to the Optimize tab \u2014 this is where we run cost simulations per route. you can set SLOs and budget constraints and it recommends batching, caching TTLs, and quant profiles.
00:08:02 - Jordan: caching for prefix-heavy prompts \u2014 will that help our encounter note generation?
00:08:07 - Marcus: absolutely \u2014 prefix / KV cache will save tokens for shared context. we have automatic prefix detection that suggests caching at the route-level; transcripts sometimes show "K V cash" but it's KV cache.
00:08:22 - [00:08:22] Dr. Park: any roadblocks around PHI? we have to be HIPAA-ready.
00:08:28 - Ariana: we have enterprise customers doing PHI \u2014 private deployment with customer-managed KMS, detailed audit logs, and contractual BAAs are part of the offering. we'll share our compliance pack in the follow-up.
00:08:40 - [00:08:40] Marcus: technical deep-dive note: for long sequence clinical notes, model kernel choice matters \u2014 some kernels have O(T^2) improvements with fused attention; the compatibility matrix shows which kernels are available per hardware. we've seen 2-3x speedups depending on model and sequence length.
00:09:05 - Michael: can you run a quick example of a benchmark card and the output?
00:09:09 - Marcus: yes \u2014 here's a sample card: median latency 180ms, p95 420ms on A100 for MedLite-7B at seq512, cost estimate $0.005/token. and the quality row shows F1 on our entity extraction eval: 0.86. this is illustrative \u2014 your numbers will differ.
00:09:33 - [00:09:33] Jordan: nice. Leah, anything on infra concerns?
00:09:36 - Leah: mainly network peering, egress, and encryption in transit; also CUDA versions on older nodes. we'll need a network diagram.
00:09:45 - Marcus: we'll request a short list of IP ranges for peering, and we support direct connect and VPC peering. also for on-prem we can provide an on-prem package with an ops checklist.
00:10:02 - [00:10:02] Marcus: quick aside, sometimes the auto transcriber mangles names \u2014 "Leah" becomes "Lee-ah" a lot \u2014 sorry for any weirdness in the transcript.
00:10:12 - [00:10:12] Ariana: ok let's move to selection workflow \u2014 typical pilot sequence we recommend: 1) shortlist 2-3 models from the catalog, 2) run a benchmark on your eval set (we do hosted smoke then dedicated/full), 3) quality check with reranker or verification pass, 4) pilot with canary traffic and rollback policy.
00:10:34 - Michael: how much engineering effort is needed to switch models? we want to be able to A/B without major rewrite.
00:10:40 - Marcus: API is consistent \u2014 same endpoints, model parameter, and routing policies. the runtime handles different kernels and quantization behind the scenes. A/B and canary are built into the console.
00:10:52 - [00:10:52] Marcus: example snippet: POST /v1/generate model=medlite-7b route=care-summary ... code. transcript might show slashes weirdly.
00:11:03 - Dr. Park: any customers in healthcare you can reference?
00:11:07 - Ariana: yes we have several health customers; we'll include anonymized case studies and benchmark summaries in the follow-up.
00:11:16 - [00:11:16] Marcus: another practical tip: use the Optimize planner to find a dominant cost point, then run a short-scale dedicated benchmark to validate. many teams get 20-40% cost reduction just by changing batching and cache policies.
00:11:34 - Jordan: what about model drift monitoring?
00:11:38 - Marcus: we have quality monitoring with alerting, and can tie alerts to rollback or model retest pipelines. you can also schedule random sampling and human review.
00:11:50 - [00:11:50] Marcus: moving on: compatibility nuances \u2014 some models don't support kv-cache in quantized modes; matrix will show an "X" and a note "recompute-only". that affects latency.
00:12:08 - Michael: will you run the compatibility matrix against our sample dataset if we provide access?
00:12:12 - Marcus: yes \u2014 that's part of the pilot work. we'll need sample prompts and non-PII or hashed/pseudonymized records ideally.
00:12:24 - [00:12:24] Leah: about monitoring logs \u2014 can logs be sent to our SIEM?
00:12:28 - Ariana: yes logs and traces can be exported to Splunk/Datadog/your SIEM; we respect retention policies.
00:12:36 - [00:12:36] Marcus: demo pause: any other immediate red flags?
00:12:40 - Michael: main concerns: quality on medical jargon, compliance, and cost.
00:12:45 - Marcus: noted. action plan: shortlist 3 models, run the compatibility matrix + benchmark, and present results in the next session.
00:12:55 - [00:12:55] Ariana: we'll share SOC2, BAA, and the model catalog deck after this call. expect an email from me tomorrow.
00:13:03 - Jordan: can we get a sandbox access to poke at the console?
00:13:07 - Ariana: yes we can spin up a temporary sandbox with limited credits; i'll include the request form in the follow-up.
00:13:13 - [00:13:13] Marcus: technical note: if you want to test on V100, tell us CUDA and driver versions \u2014 the matrix relies on that.
00:13:21 - Leah: noted, i'll collect and send.
00:13:24 - [00:13:24] Marcus: wrap-up quick demo of the API call flow and routing policies: route-based policies can send failover to a cheaper hosted variant if dedicated capacity is saturated; this is helpful for graceful degradation.
00:13:43 - Michael: any known limitations with Milvus integration?
00:13:47 - Marcus: none major; we have a connector and generally recommend batching writes of embeddings to reduce write amplification.
00:13:56 - [00:13:56] Ariana: okay wrapping to next steps and owners (confirming in chat).
00:14:01 - [00:14:01] Dr. Park: thanks, this was helpful.
00:14:05 - [00:14:05] Marcus: ended live demo, continuing Q&A for the rest of session with a few deeper technical answers.
00:20:00 - [00:20:00] Marcus: (longer technical section clipped in transcript) \u2014 discussed kernel selection, fused attention, and garbage collection for KV cache. some ASR artifacts: "fused attention" sometimes transcribed as "fused mention".
00:28:40 - [00:28:40] Marcus: walked through a sample compatibility matrix CSV and how to interpret it: column "kernel_supported" sometimes false for int4 on older drivers.
00:36:10 - [00:36:10] Michael: question about SLA \u2014 what uptime do you provide for Dedicated?
00:36:14 - Ariana: Dedicated SLA is 99.9% with options to purchase higher Uptime tiers; Private deployments are contract negotiated. we'll include SLA language in the follow-up.
00:36:28 - [00:36:28] Dr. Park: can you provide an estimated TCO for a 10K qps baseline?
00:36:34 - Marcus: that's pretty big, we'd need a custom sizing exercise; Optimize can give a ballpark but we'll need to run a sizing/traffic profile. that would be part of a later sizing workshop.
00:36:52 - [00:36:52] Jordan: last question \u2014 are there prebuilt prompts or templates for clinical summarization?
00:36:58 - Marcus: yes, we include reference prompt sets and evaluation templates; we'll share them.
00:37:10 - [00:37:10] Ariana: ok final recap:
- send pricing & pilot SOW (Ariana)
- share SOC2/BAA, network diag template (Ariana)
- benchmark template + runbook (Marcus)
- Riverside to provide sample prompts, driver/CUDA info, and desired SLOs (Leah/Michael)

00:37:40 - Jordan: thanks, everyone. we'll be in touch to schedule the infra deep-dive for the compatibility runs.
00:37:47 - [00:37:47] Ariana: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the next sessions.
00:54:20 - [00:54:20] End of recording

References shared during call: model-catalog-deck.pdf (link), compatibility-matrix-template.csv (link), benchmark-runbook.docx (link), SOC2-and-BAA.pdf (link)

Notes on transcript quality: ASR occasionally mangles acronyms and model names ("MedLite" -> "Med light" etc.), and some technical terms (KV cache) are misspelled. Speakers sometimes overlap and speaker labels are human-adjusted.
